statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) in every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 69 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour of this window and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs 25 to 32 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack. No danger window is defined.
headline: Weekend halt, hour twenty: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, an unresolved hawkish Warsh repricing with the 2-year at 4.35% against a semiconductor-led Friday decline
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August and the scheduled reopen falls about seven hours beyond the final slot of this window. Pre-halt evidence was re-verified against primary sources this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The dominant Friday driver remains Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, read as hawkish: the 2-year yield rose about 11 basis points to 4.350 percent, its highest in a month, within a 4.216 to 4.360 percent range, while the 10-year added about 5 basis points to 4.72 percent and September rate-hike odds moved to roughly 57 to 60 percent from about 35 percent. The decline was narrow rather than broad: all seven tracked semiconductors closed lower with a mean change near minus 2.5 percent, led by Arm down 6.33 percent and Nvidia down 4.57 percent, while five of eight tracked megacaps advanced, with Amazon up 3.97 percent, Alphabet up 1.74 percent and Microsoft up 1.68 percent, leaving megacap dispersion near 2.5 percentage points. Sector context was split, with Technology about 1.4 percent lower against Communication Services and Consumer Cyclical each about 1.4 percent higher. The same repricing was expressed in a dollar index gain of roughly 0.6 percent to near 99.66 and a gold decline of more than 2.5 percent from a 4,629 dollar high, while crude softened with WTI settling at 83.40 dollars, down 0.16 percent in an 82.25 to 83.78 dollar range, with no verified new Middle East supply discontinuity. Delayed cross-asset context showed Treasury futures lower across the curve and the volatility future higher, consistent with that read but explicitly not usable as live price-path evidence. Weekend headline flow through the assessment cutoff has been thematic rather than index-moving, with no verified geopolitical or policy discontinuity. Because Tail measures a persistent no-retracement price path and no venue is open to produce one, Tail is 5 in every hour of this window and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with no danger window; Stress runs 25 to 32 in the moderate band purely as a measure of information waiting to be priced at the reopen and ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence steps down from 69 to 63 as a function of tape age rather than conflicting evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the final four hours of Friday's cash session and the first twenty hours of the weekend halt. The mode was event/whipsaw as the Jackson Hole keynote hit the tape, and Tail peaked at 22 with Stress at 64 in the 16:00 to 19:00 UTC block; the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH because retracements kept occurring throughout the repricing. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the readings decayed quickly, Tail from 12 to 5 and Stress from 52 to 25, as the venue entered its weekend closure and the mode reverted to normal. Every hour of this window has a published assessment. The twenty halt hours sit at a flat Tail of 5 with Stress in the low to mid twenties, and Confidence steps down from 88 to 70 purely as a function of tape age.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form; Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress runs 25 to 32 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates: the unresolved hawkish policy read with the 2-year at 4.35 percent and September hike odds around 57 to 60 percent, Friday's narrow semiconductor-led decline with Arm down 6.33 percent and Nvidia down 4.57 percent against five of eight megacaps higher, the dollar and gold moves that expressed the same repricing, the softer crude path near 83 dollars WTI, Broadcom's fiscal Q3 report scheduled after the close on 2 September, and the 1 to 4 September data stack running from ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS through ADP and ISM Services to Nonfarm Payrolls. Confidence eases from 69 to 63 as the reference tape ages. The first genuine price-path evidence arrives at the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen, roughly seven hours after the final slot of this window.
